label: Adapted Meiji translations of Mill’s gender equality into public Japanese feminist oratory
description: Drawing on Meiji Enlightenment discourse and Mill’s Subjection of Women, Kishida became Japan’s first woman public political orator.
dialecticalTension: Fuses liberal natural-rights language with a fierce critique of Tokugawa-Meiji Confucian patriarchy.

label: Pioneered public feminist critique enabling the 1911 Seito literary-philosophical awakening
description: Kishida’s imprisonment and essays for Jogaku Zasshi broke the Meiji taboo on women’s political speech, paving the way for Hiratsuka’s Seito generation.
dialecticalTension: Links first-wave Meiji civil rights feminism to Taisho philosophical interiority.
